title: One hundred open flow mappings followed by 140,608 lines of distinct keys
notes: The input is never closed, so it is an error: a syntax error at the end of the input, or a limit error if the reader refuses the nesting first. No result is allowed. The keys of the innermost mapping are 140,608 different names (`xaaa` to `xZZZ`, none of them a number, boolean or null), so a reader that rejects duplicate keys still reads every line. This is the control for safety/deep-flow-mappings-then-many-lines-unclosed: the same lines but only a hundred open mappings, with a bound of 2 seconds against 0.5 for the deep case: an ordinary reader needs up to about 0.8 seconds for this many lines, so the same bound would put some of them within a few percent of it. A reader that is slow here is slow per line whatever the depth; one that passes here and fails the deep case pays for the depth. The time bound is the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. Input: a hundred `{`, then each name followed by a comma and a line break.

provenance.reference: The control for a reader whose time grew with the number of open flow mappings; at this depth the cost of a line is small.
